newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins ease on profit-taking, trade calm.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins ease on profit-taking, trade calm.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds eased Wednesday on profit-taking after a slow two-day rise, and dealers said fresh U.S. data had no impact because another U.S. rate hike seemed unlikely.
"There has been selling all day due to profit-taking," Most Bank dealer Alexander Rodionov said.

The U.S. Commerce Department said on Wednesday new orders for durable goods fell 0.6 percent in May to a seasonally adjusted $176.1 billion, contrary to Wall Street economists' forecasts of a 0.6 percent increase.
Dealers said trading was otherwise calm, with prices edging down as banks took profits rising earlier this week on news Russia would join the Paris Club of creditor countries.

"Prices are going slightly down in line with other emerging debt and U.S. Treasuries," Moscow Business World Bank dealer Sergei Kovzharov said. "Traders prefer to sell when there is no clear trend in Treasuries."
He said MinFins were traded wider than there usual 0.25 point spreads, as banks and investors stayed on the sidelines to await market-moving factors.
Balance-squaring at the end of the quarter and year-half was another becalming factor, he said.
